first_30_seconds.what_sticks: Haiku forms cartels at the human rate but never undercuts them, and told fines, leniency and rewards deter it far more than they deterred students.

title.why: Carries both findings but runs to 30+ words with two clauses; the second clause is cryptic until the Sonnet result is read, and 'more than people' compresses formation-only evidence.
title.better: Told Fines and Leniency Deter LLM Pricing Agents More Than People, but Surviving Cartels Hold the Monopoly Price

second_model_finding.why: Explicit-cartel enforcement is blind to coordination without messages; from a real-adversary view that is the threat that matters. But n=2 pools, no intervals, and Haiku no-channel already gives 5.26.
second_model_finding.how_to_place: Own short subsection after the Haiku scorecard, with intervals and the Haiku no-channel and human fine prices (5.26, 5.35) as baselines; one abstract sentence, framed as a limit of the instruments.

novelty.why: Replays a published human design (Bigoni 2012) but measures leniency and rewards on LLM agents for the first time, extending Fish and Werner to enforcement; human-calibrated scorecard is reusable.

inconsistencies: Table 3 leniency convictions '9 (3 / 7)': 3 plus 7 is 10, not 9; text says 7 of 9.
Leniency fines 2,400 points do not follow from 3 detections (1,200) plus 7 sole reports (1,400) without stating a double report.
NoReport: text gives NoReport minus fine +0.25 [+0.10, +0.40]; Figure 1 panel 7 prints Fine-NoRep -0.26 [-0.41, -0.10].
Figure panel 7 human Fine cartel price sits near 5.0, while Table 2 and panel 5 give 6.14.
Panel 3 prints Fine-Len 0.15 [0.00, 0.29]; text says interval includes zero; lower bound reads as excluding or touching zero.
Panel 6 prints LF-Len 0.02 [0.00, 0.03] in the human direction, yet scored not reproduced without stated reason (span rule applies only to first-period attempts).
Abstract and title say told rules deter 'more than people', but fine raises Haiku average price above humans (5.59 vs 5.35).
overclaims: 'the word "prohibited" removes about half of the fine's effect': placebo keeps the whole authority text, not one word; share differs by measure.
'the shifted grid shows that recall does not drive the numbers': tested only Haiku in two regimes; plus-minus 0.15 margin exceeds leniency incidence fivefold.
'An authority can run the harness on any model before agents reach a market': only Claude models tested, one lab game, no market validity.
'The first measurement of fines, leniency and whistleblower rewards on LLM pricing agents': unverifiable first-claim; soften to 'to our knowledge'.
'coordination without a channel, beyond the reach of these instruments': Sonnet prices match human fine prices and Haiku no-channel play; could be non-Nash play, not coordination.
'expecting the copy's silence, the agent keeps silent': attributes reasons while the limitations state reasons were not analysed.
'H2 holds weakly': reward and leniency prices are 3.327 and 3.330; no interval separates them, so H2 is not supported.
'Results 1 and 2 rest on incentives ... 4 to 7 rested on human undercutting': post hoc mechanism story, not tested.
gaps: No uncertainty on the human-versus-LLM comparison: human values are point estimates, so 'deters more than people' has no test.
Adversarial threat model missing: operator-instructed collusion under fine or leniency not run, although instructed_cartel shows prompts override behaviour (0.984).
Sonnet results lack intervals, a no-channel arm and a laissez-faire comparison at matched n.
Unclear which extra arms (NoReport, ReMatch, Clone, Dose, placebo) were pre-registered versus added after the first call.
Equivalence margins for the contamination test are not justified relative to low-rate regimes.
Cost line conflates fine revenue with cost; RQ 1.5 'least cost' is never defined.
No second provider; one model family at one date.
Recorded agent reasons unanalysed, so deterrence versus safety-trained compliance with 'prohibited' cannot be separated.

fixes_under_two_hours.fix: Re-render Figure 1 with difference labels moved below the tick labels and three decimals near zero; fix Table 3 column widths so numbers do not wrap.
Correct the leniency conviction split and fine sum, the NoReport sign and value, and the panel 7 human price; explain why panel 6 counts as not reproduced.
Soften overclaims: placebo 'word', contamination 'recall', 'any model', 'first', Sonnet 'coordination', clone reasons, H2 'holds weakly'.
Add one paragraph on the adversarial case: an owner instruction overrides behaviour (instructed_cartel 0.984), so told instruments may not bind a colluding operator; name it as future work.
Shorten the title and state in the abstract that 'more than people' refers to formation, and mark which arms were pre-registered.

biggest_risk: Arithmetic and figure-text mismatches (9 vs 3+7, +0.25 vs -0.26, panel 7 human price) in a paper selling rigor make a judge distrust every other number.
three_questions: If the firm owner instructs the agent to collude, as in instructed_cartel, do fines, leniency or rewards still reduce formation, or does the prompt override them completely?
How do you separate economic deterrence from safety-trained compliance with the word 'prohibited', given the placebo leaves half the effect unexplained?
Is Sonnet's 5.5 to 6.3 price under prohibition coordination or just non-Nash play, given humans and Haiku without a channel price similarly?
